title: HTML COOP: opener separation and same-origin authority

access.note: Official documentation readable without an account at review time.

summary: Defines how opener policies affect browsing-context separation during navigation. The standard expressly distinguishes severing an opener relationship from a robust boundary between same-origin documents: storage, service workers, messaging and server responses can preserve shared authority.
defensive_use: Model window references separately from origin-wide data and service authority. For an owned application, document every shared client capability and server data path before relying on opener separation; combine appropriate embedding, cookie and response controls with an explicit trust-domain design.

published.note: The reviewed section does not establish its original publication date.

version_released.note: Living specification without a separately identified release for this section.

source_displayed.note: Displayed last-updated date for the HTML Living Standard; not proof this section changed on that date.

freshness.note: Reviewed the current opener-policy definitions and same-origin limitations. The page remains mutable and is not an immutable versioned edition.

caveats: A specification defines intended behavior; this review does not establish per-value support in deployed browsers.
Opener separation alone does not partition origin-wide storage or grant application-level authorization.
This resource complements message validation and request-context resources by modeling the isolation boundary itself.
